categories.title: Quantum information
categories.summary: Quantum light sources and photon-pair generation in two-dimensional materials.

topics.title: Quantum light sources
topics.description: We study localized emitters and nonclassical light in two-dimensional materials. Moire confinement and nanostructures provide ways to control their emission and optical coupling.

outcomes.title: Energy-tunable quantum light from moire-trapped excitons
Spin and charge control of moire-trapped excitons and trions
Photoexcitation of moire-trapped excitons via chiral phonons

topics.mappingNote: All six papers are retained from the original Quantum information related-paper list. The phonon, spin and charge papers support the material platform; do not describe every paper as demonstrating single-photon emission.

topics.title: SPDC in 2D materials
topics.description: We investigate photon-pair generation through spontaneous parametric down-conversion in nonlinear two-dimensional materials, including the role of layer stacking and twist angle.
topics.claimLimit: The Wix SPDC detail page contains a conceptual diagram and research description, but no linked publication. Do not invent a demonstrated entangled-photon result or attach unrelated group papers as SPDC evidence.
topics.summary: We investigate photon-pair generation through spontaneous parametric down-conversion in nonlinear two-dimensional materials, including the role of layer stacking and twist angle.

categories.title: Solid-State Physics
categories.summary: Moiré potentials, correlated states and electrically controlled interlayer excitons.

topics.title: Moiré physics
topics.description: Twist angle and lattice mismatch create periodic potentials in stacked two-dimensional materials. We study localized excitons and field-tunable correlated electronic states.

outcomes.title: Exciton-polarons in a correlated moire superlattice
Field-tunable correlated states in a multi-orbital moire system

topics.summary: Twist angle and lattice mismatch create periodic potentials in stacked two-dimensional materials. We study localized excitons and field-tunable correlated electronic states.

topics.title: Interlayer excitons
topics.description: Electrons and holes in separate layers form excitons whose optical response can be controlled by electric fields. We study dipolar, quadrupolar and symmetric excitonic states.

outcomes.title: Tunable ground- and excited-state excitonic dipoles
Quadrupolar and dipolar excitons in bilayer MoSe2
Symmetric interlayer trions in MoS2 bilayers

topics.claimLimit: Spatial trapping as a quantum simulator and exciton-polariton devices are presented as applications/directions on the original detail page. Do not claim a completed simulator or polariton device from these three papers.
topics.summary: Electrons and holes in separate layers form excitons whose optical response can be controlled by electric fields. We study dipolar, quadrupolar and symmetric excitonic states.
